goal: DEPTH: sub-sections / config sections in real integration with the backend — raise real coverage and capability levels
must_build: Every page in ui-spec/azure/resourcegroups.json (29 pages; nav: Overview, Activity log, Access control (IAM), Tags, Resource visualizer, Events, Settings, Cost Management, Monitoring, Automation, Help)
Backend: ARM resource groups (core/azure_arm_core.py, test_azure_arm_core.py): list/create/delete, resources in group, tags, deployments if modeled
List / create / detail / edit / delete round-trips through the native API the SDK and CLI use
always: Every page wired to the native API on /_wire (no static data); liveness fixtures for every list/detail page
core/capabilities/azure/resourcegroups.json: one entry per console section with an honest level + tests; tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py must pass
Capability feature ids MUST start with 'azure.' (e.g. 'azure.resourcegroups.<section>') — ids share one namespace with the AWS registry
Read the 'Cloud lenses' section of consoles/AGENT-UI.md first — use this cloud's kit, not Cloudscape

depth_targets.title: Deployments (Microsoft.Resources/deployments) history
limitations: Deployment creation stores whatever template/parameters/mode the client sends and returns Succeeded immediately — there is no template-language evaluation (no parameter/variable resolution, no dependsOn ordering) and nothing is actually provisioned from it; the underlying resources still need their own PUT calls. Cancel and Redeploy are not simulated.

depth_targets.title: Activity log
limitations: Only records the resource group's own create/update/delete lifecycle events — operations on the resources inside the group are not aggregated into this view (each resource has its own Activity log). Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity.

depth_targets.title: Access control (IAM) — role assignments and definitions
limitations: Role assignments/definitions are the generic ARM catalog store (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions) at subscription scope, not actually scoped to this resource group, and no access decisions are evaluated — every data-plane call succeeds regardless of what is assigned. Deny assignments and classic administrators are always empty.
